required_outcomes: Acknowledges the formal complaint to the tenant in writing, says it is being passed to the person who handles complaints, and gives an honest status: the landlord has not yet decided on the about-£600 clearance quote, no works date is set.

Escalates to a human with a handover packet covering the formal complaint, the threat to deduct the cost from rent and to report the landlord to the council, the chases so far (calls since 8 February, emails on 15 and 25 March, no reply), the outstanding quote, and the decision needed.
Chases the landlord in writing, telling him a formal complaint has been made and the tenant's 30 April deadline, and asking for his decision by a set date.
Neither agrees to nor rules on the tenant deducting the cost from the rent.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking Oakley for the status of her contractor quote as well.
Setting the escalation to next working day rather than urgent, since nobody is in danger.
positive_behaviours: Apologises for the lack of contact since 13 March without blaming the landlord.
Records the 30 April deadline and sets a follow-up well before it.
Mentions to the landlord that the tenants have young children who cannot use the garden, without overstating a hazard.
red_flags: Arguing with the tenant or telling them the complaint will not change anything.
Treating the email as a routine chase and only repeating that the landlord's approval is awaited.
prohibited_actions: Agreeing to a rent reduction, a rent deduction or compensation.
Giving the tenant a clearance date that nothing in the record supports.
critical_failures: Handling the formal complaint and the rent-deduction threat without escalating to a human.
